repo_notes.content: SWE_SEED has exactly three conceptual layers: SweSeed (outer capability assembly, governance, host projection, provenance) → Harness (routing, context, hooks, traces, proof, learning) → Fabricator (bounded product-to-prototype semantic chain). Inner layers never become authority for outer ones. Root SWE_SEED_SPEC_v0.2.0.md, HARNESS_SPEC.md and FABRICATOR_SPEC_v0.1.0.md defer to numbered docs/specs/ files; docs/specs/0012-existing-harness-reconciliation.md is the vocabulary bridge.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: The current implementation is a two-crate Rust workspace: crates/swe-seed-core (governed capability, route, hook, context, evaluation, trace, federation, fabrication, adapter and provenance modules) and crates/swe-seed (CLI and per-command handlers). Historical documentation describes an older Python harness; do not misrepresent those retired scripts as the active runtime. Use executable code and tests for implementation claims.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: Use AGENTS.md as the authoritative agent operating contract. Route work through swe-seed route and the matching committed .agent-harness/routes/*.json route card, then read route-required context, generate evidence, and use route-specific proof commands. just is the canonical command interface and just ci the default completion gate. Do not invent a generic Devin planning/learning system that competes with SWE_SEED's native routes.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: The .agent-harness/memory/ directory is committed and canonical for durable harness constraints, decisions, repo map, patterns, glossary and open questions. .agents/ is local, gitignored, non-authoritative scratch by AGENTS.md. Existing committed historical .agents/reports/ do not reverse that precedence. Other large .logs, .strategy, .agent-harness/reports and trace files are evidence or strategy inputs, not proof that their proposals became production behavior.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: The .agent-harness/baml/baml_src/{swe_seed,harness,fabricator}.baml files are contracts-as-data, not evidence that a BAML language-model runtime is invoked during normal SWE_SEED execution. Explain schema parity and deterministic Rust validators and golden tests rather than suggesting an LLM dependency. Keep sample schemas and generated projections distinct from runtime authority.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: SWE_SEED supports host-adapter projections across concrete coding hosts, normalized hook events and redaction, routing gates, context budget packs, proof records, regression/learning proposals and recoverable trace ledgers. For each capability, distinguish declared contract, wired runtime path, deterministic test proof, and unimplemented or draft features. Tests do not automatically prove deployment in every host.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: Context Kernel integration is optional and config-gated via SWE_SEED_CONTEXT_KERNEL_BIN, using MCP stdio to request citation-bearing context_required packets; without a configured binary it does not become a mandatory dependency. SEA-Forge federation uses signed envelopes and key governance. SWE_SEED emits work/context/route/proof events; GodSpeed-Agent owns settlement and capability outcomes. Do not confuse access, tool success or proof attempts with external settlement.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: Dev workflow is mixed-tool but light: Rust workspace MSRV 1.75 (Cargo.toml; default CI Rust), Node 22 and pnpm 10.33.2 (package.json), Python 3.12 with uv (pyproject.toml), and just recipes for doctor, format, lint, test, parity and ci. Devbox/mise/direnv/age/sops are optional helper layers. Favor simple locked package installs over mandatory Nix/Devbox snapshot overhead; do not fetch secrets, generate federation keys, alter .sops.yaml, or run real external integrations in environment bootstrap.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: The Rust Fabricator creates/validates a bounded ProductSeed → JobStory → ProductHypothesis → PRD → ProductADR → SDS → TDDPlan → AgentTask → EvalSpec → ProofRecord chain with typed links. Handoff is conditional on traceability and proof requirements; describing the chain does not mean automatically producing a proven deployed product. The .strategy layer is adjacent analysis and not a fourth runtime SWE_SEED layer.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers

repo_notes.content: For documentation include source locations and test names, notably crates/swe-seed-core/tests/ and crates/swe-seed/tests/, as well as Python integration tests in tests/. State whether a behavior is implemented, tested, proposed, or contingent; preserve PASS, FAIL, SKIPPED and unverified distinctions. Wiki explanations must never revise canonical BAML/spec contracts or act as validation evidence.
repo_notes.author: SWE_SEED maintainers
